title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong with the surrounding handwritten notes. It is a typed page (numbered '- 23 -', filed upside down) from a typescript on the cohomology of sites. It has nothing to do with the abelian-variety and cycle-class computations on the neighbouring pages (u_*(1_A), Λ^• T_ℓ, degree d).

In modern terms, the content is as follows.

- **Setting.** u: C → C' is a continuous functor between sites. Its restriction functor (here called the 'direct image') sends a sheaf F' on C' to u^s F' = F'∘u, a sheaf on C.
- **Definition (presumed).** 'C-acyclic' means H^q(X, F) = 0 for all q > 0 and all objects X of C. By the cited 2.6, this notion depends only on the underlying abelian sheaf.
- **Warning.** The restriction of a C'-acyclic sheaf need not be C-acyclic.
- **Proposition 3.3.** Assume condition (CMG); the 'G' is almost certainly a typewritten 'C', so read (CMC), roughly 'compatibility with fibre products on covering families'. The condition is: every covering sieve R of X contains the sieve generated by a covering family (U_i → X) such that
  1. the iterated fibre products U_{i1} ×_X … ×_X U_{in} exist in C;
  2. the corresponding fibre products of the u(U_i) over u(X) exist in C';
  3. u carries the former isomorphically onto the latter.

  This holds for instance when C has fibre products and u commutes with them. Conclusion: u^s of any C'-acyclic sheaf is C-acyclic.
- **Proof idea (implicit).**
  - Because u is continuous, (u(U_i) → u(X)) is a covering family in C'.
  - Condition 3 gives an isomorphism of Čech complexes Č(U_•/X, u^s F') ≅ Č(u(U_•)/u(X), F').
  - For an acyclic F', the Čech cohomology of any covering family vanishes in positive degree.
  - Hence u^s F' has vanishing higher Čech cohomology on a system of coverings cofinal in all covering sieves.
  - By Cartan's criterion (as in SGA 4 V), u^s F' is then acyclic.

This is the standard behaviour of acyclic sheaves under morphisms of sites, as treated in SGA 4 Exposé V (Verdier) and related typescripts on site/topos cohomology.
errors: Typos only: 'G"' should read 'G' (or 'C'); 'tel que' should read 'telle que'.
The proposition itself appears correct; it rests on Cartan's Čech criterion for acyclicity, which is cited only implicitly.

ideas.what: Restriction along a continuous functor preserves acyclic sheaves provided the functor is compatible with fibre products of a cofinal system of covering families.
ideas.modern_name: Preservation of acyclicity under pushforward along a morphism of sites, via Čech complexes and Cartan's criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verdier / Grothendieck, SGA 4 Exposé V (Cartan's lemma goes back to H. Cartan)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé V (Cohomologie dans les topos), §4: Čech cohomology and acyclicity criteria

ideas.what: Acyclicity depends only on the underlying abelian sheaf, not on the ring of scalars.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the forgetful functor from modules to abelian sheaves with cohomology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled typed page of a standard exposition of site cohomology, apparently an SGA 4 V-type typescript. The result is well known and has no connection to the cycle and abelian-variety notes around it.
transcription_corrections: The page is scanned upside down; it is typed, not handwritten.
'G-acyclicité' and 'G-acyclique', and the sites 'G, G'', are most likely 'C-acyclicité' and 'C, C'' (typewritten C); likewise the condition is probably labelled '(CMC)' rather than '(CMG)'.
'restriction à G"' should read 'restriction à G' (or C).
'tel que le crible' should read 'telle que le crible'.
